reasons.plausibility: Graphite and MoS2 oxidize or degrade well below 800 °C in air, so they cannot provide lubrication across the full temperature range as proposed.
reasons.testability: The proposed pin-on-disk test with friction and wear measurements is clear, but the falsification criterion is weak because it lacks a quantitative threshold and does not address the known high-temperature failure of the lubricants.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is too generic and ignores the well-known temperature limitations of graphite and MoS2, so it does not offer a viable path for a researcher working on this specific high-temperature challenge.
